text:
anna_ml: Heads up — we're onboarding Murre-3B (MurreAI v1.0) into evals. Found the license looks like a research/non-commercial variant and there's an ambiguous hosting/redistribution clause. Can someone legal weigh in? cc @mike_legal @sara_research

anna_ml: Relevant excerpt: ```License Section 3.b: "Model weights and derivative models shall not be commercially redistributed or hosted for third-party inference without explicit commercial license from the rights holder."```

mike_legal: Thanks — short answer: that wording typically blocks running the model as a commercial hosted inference service (i.e., Dedicated/Hosted) unless we buy a commercial license. Need to confirm whether 'derivative models' explicitly includes quantized weights.

sara_research: From an ML standpoint, quantized weights are almost always considered derivatives because they transform the original tensor values. So distributing Q-weights (even to customers in a Private package) would likely be "redistribution." :thinking:

dave_infra: To be concrete for infra planning: if the customer runs in Redwood Dedicated (we manage the GPUs) and we load the Murre weights under a research-only constraint, that smells like hosting. Customers pay for inference; seems disallowed per that clause.

anna_ml: Two user stories we need to decide: 1) internal evals / benchmarking (OK under research), 2) allow customers to use Murre via our Hosted API or Dedicated (likely not allowed), 3) Private on-prem package where customer runs weights in their infra (maybe allowed?).

mike_legal: On-prem where customer holds the binary is usually fine if the upstream license permits redistribution to the customer. But the clause says 'no commercial redistribution or hosting' — it's ambiguous whether supplying a customer a copy (Private deployment tarball) counts as redistribution. We'll ask upstream. I'll open a vendor request and flag commercial license needed for any customer-facing product.

license-bot: New vendor request created: VR-2026-031 — MurreAI licensing clarification (assigned to @mike_legal). See: https://vendor-requests.internal/VR-2026-031 :eyes:

sara_research: Another angle: what about embeddings/outputs? Some licenses restrict outputs (e.g., embeddings) only if they contain verbatim model material. If the license restricts "hosting/redistribution" but not downstream outputs, we might be able to provide embeddings as a feature without redistributing weights. But that's license-specific.

anna_ml: Adding audit/bench artifacts to the vendor request. Note: quantization impact is non-trivial — quick bench from our int8 experiment: `squad-f1 baseline float32=0.812`, `int8=0.795` (drop ~1.7 pts). Customers using retrieval/qa might notice regressions.

dave_infra: Logging note: quantization pipeline used `quantize.py --mode int8 --perchannel` and produced a qweights tarball at `s3://redwood-models/murre3b/int8/v1/qweights.tar.gz`. If the license forbids redistribution, we must ensure that tarball is restricted to internal evals only and not shipped to customers.

mike_legal: Plan: 1) Mark Murre-3B as "research-only" in model-catalog and block Dedicated/Hosted deploys for now. 2) File vendor request and ask upstream for a commercial license and clarification on whether quantized weights or packaged containers count as "redistribution." 3) Ask whether outputs/embeddings are covered.

anna_ml: I'll update the onboarding checklist and tag the model as blocked for production. Also adding eval artifacts and the quantization regression graphs to VR-2026-031.

sara_research: FYI we'll also run a light-weight A/B on int8 vs fp16 on representative prompts to produce signal for legal (how visible the regression is). Might help negotiations if we can show workable fallbacks.

mike_legal: Good. I'll ping MurreAI legal and loop in partnerships for pricing. For now: do not provision Murre-3B to any customer-facing pools, do not ship quantized weights to customers, and treat embeddings as 'hold until clarified'. :thumbsup:

anna_ml: Got it — thanks everyone.

dave_infra: Echoing — locking down S3 paths and IAM for those qweights now.

license-bot: VR-2026-031 updated: attachments added (bench graphs, quantize.log).
